one_liner: 2D rigid-body physics engine in C17; the unreleased v3.2 steps the same scenes about 2x faster than v3.1.1.
what_it_does: Box2D simulates 2D rigid bodies: circles, capsules, convex and rounded polygons, segments and chains, with joints, continuous collision, sensors, contact events, island sleep, and ray, shape and overlap queries. v3 is a C rewrite with an ID-based (handle) API: b2CreateWorld, b2CreateBody, b2CreatePolygonShape, b2World_Step(worldId, dt, subSteps). Its baseline here is its own previous release v3.1.1, so this is an in-place upgrade within the v3 API family rather than a replacement for another engine; v2.4 users face a full migration.
how_it_is_fast: Data-oriented storage with a sub-stepping 'Soft Step' solver over graph-colored constraint batches, solved several bodies wide with SIMD: SSE2, Neon or WASM simd128, plus an 8-wide AVX2 contact solver that v3.2 compiles by default and picks at runtime from the CPU id. Multithreading runs on a built-in task scheduler (or user task callbacks) across collision, solver stages and island splitting. Per performance_v320.md, the v3.2 gains come mostly from engine work visible even on SSE2 (faster SAT, cache and broad-phase work, faster island splitting, contact recycling, a size-relative AABB margin that creates fewer contacts, lower scheduler overhead), with about 10% more from AVX2.
when_to_use: 2D games or simulations with large stacks and piles of bodies, where v3.2 gained about 2.7-3.0x over v3.1.1 (large_pyramid, many_pyramids, sleep, junkyard).
Multicore desktops: set b2WorldDef::workerCount (up to B2_MAX_WORKERS) to use the built-in scheduler, or plug in your own job system through enqueueTask/finishTask.
x86-64 machines with AVX2, where the 8-wide contact solver is picked at runtime with no build flag.
Rollback or lockstep networking: b2World_GetStateHash is documented to reproduce across worker counts, and snapshot/recording APIs exist for save games and replays.
Existing v3.0/v3.1 users who can take main-branch code and some API changes.
when_not_to_use: 3D physics: Box2D is 2D only; use Jolt, Bullet or PhysX.
Query-bound workloads (heavy ray casts, shape casts, overlap queries): queries and tree_cast gained only 1.17-1.31x, and those calls run on the calling thread, so they do not scale with threads.
Projects that need a tagged, stable release: v3.2 is unreleased (latest tag v3.1.1, 2025-06-04), and the v3.2 API differs enough that the benchmark scenes had to be ported to v3.1.1.
Projects on v2.4 that depend on its behaviour or C++ API: v3 is a rewrite whose behaviour changed, and the migration guide recommends v3 for new projects.
Very stiff or unstable joint assemblies: open bug #984 (crash with prismatic joints) is, per the author, a setup the solver cannot handle.

integration.form: static lib (CMake; shared builds through BUILD_SHARED_LIBS), C API; also consumable from Zig and Swift Package Manager
integration.dependencies: none for the library (v3.2 has a built-in task scheduler; v3.1.1 needed enkiTS or your own scheduler for multithreading); samples need a C++20 compiler plus the bundled GLFW/imgui
integration.min_toolchain: C17 compiler, CMake 3.22+ (MSVC, GCC, Clang; the measured build was MSVC 19.51)
integration.platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS; x86-64 (SSE2 baseline, AVX2 picked at runtime), AArch64 Neon, WebAssembly (simd128); BOX2D_DISABLE_SIMD gives a scalar build and BOX2D_DOUBLE_PRECISION a large-world build
integration.thread_safety: A world is not safe for concurrent writes; the engine multithreads internally per world through workerCount or user task callbacks. Custom allocator (b2SetAllocator) and assert callbacks must be thread-safe.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same v3 C API family as v3.1.1, but v3.2 changed some API (the scenes needed porting), moved multithreading to the built-in scheduler, and creates fewer contacts, so contact events and behaviour can differ

gotchas: Harness finding: the v3.1.1 baseline column used 'default CMake options for each version', and in v3.1.1 the default leaves BOX2D_AVX2 OFF (an optional compile-time 8-wide AVX2 contact solver). So v3.2's runtime AVX2 kernels were compared against a 4-wide SSE2 build of v3.1.1, and the ISA-matched figures are the page's SSE2-forced row: 1.83x on 1 thread and 2.03x on 8. In the v3.1-era 7950X CSVs (commit d5935a7), the AVX2 build was 1.18x (large_pyramid), 1.11x (many_pyramids) and 1.13x (tumbler) faster than SSE2 on one thread (derived from page data), so the 2.85-2.96x per-scene headlines overstate the like-for-like gain on AVX2 machines.

Harness finding: the headline column is labelled 'world capacity set from b2World_GetMaxCapacity', but the public benchmark/main.c never sets b2WorldDef::capacity. It reproduces the 2.03x/2.18x 'default' row rather than 2.04x/2.19x (the difference is negligible). The v3.1.1 port of the 14 scenes is not published, so the baseline column cannot be rerun from public code.

v3.2 sizes the broad-phase AABB margin relative to shape size, so it creates fewer contacts (washer 29k against 42k, tumbler 8.6k against 11k). The per-step work differs from v3.1.1, and so can contact begin/end event timing.

Soft Step sub-stepping applies velocity or impulse changes only on the first sub-step, so control bodies with forces or make them kinematic. b2World_EnableSSE2Fallback is documented as a testing switch; use the CMake option BOX2D_AVX2=OFF in production.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among the catalogued physics siblings, Jolt, Bullet, ODE, PhysX and Simbody are 3D engines, so Box2D v3 is the pick for 2D. PlayRho's catalogued wins were measured against Box2D 2.4.1, not v3, so for new 2D work on a maintained, multithreaded SIMD engine choose Box2D v3.
verified_claims_summary: A first-party self-comparison: on the 14 scenes in shared/benchmarks.c (60 Hz, 4 sub-steps, summed time of all steps after the first, minimum of four runs), main-branch v3.2 built with MSVC 19.51 Release took 2.04x less time than v3.1.1 on one thread and 2.19x less on eight, in geometric mean. The run was on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D under Windows 11 with turbo disabled, pinned one thread per core. The baseline was a default (SSE2-only) v3.1.1 build running an unpublished port of the scenes; with both versions on SSE2 the gain is 1.83x and 2.03x.
status_note: Actively developed (benchmark page and AVX2 runtime dispatch landed 2026-10-04) and MIT-licensed, but v3.2 is main-branch code with no release tag yet. The evidence is a first-party self-comparison whose baseline was built without v3.1.1's optional AVX2 path, so read the ISA-matched 1.83x/2.03x rather than the 2.04x/2.19x headline.
